title: Read the Intent Taxonomy
subtitle: The governed category tree
scenario: Before you can classify a ticket, you need the governed category tree it maps to. Read Relay's intent taxonomy - the owned set of categories with their definitions - and record it. Classification maps to these categories, never to invented free-text labels.
input:
Relay's intent taxonomy (owned by the Support Ops Analyst) has four top categories:
outage - service down for many users
bug - a feature broken for some users
how-to - a usage question, nothing broken
billing - invoices, payments, plan changes
Record each category with its definition.
instructions: Create one row per taxonomy category.
Record each category with its governed definition.
Use the categories exactly: outage, bug, how-to, billing.
Return a JSON array of the four rows, then validate.

expectedRows.definition: a feature broken for some users

copilotPrompt: Record the intent taxonomy as a JSON array: one row per category (outage, bug, how-to, billing) with its governed definition.
successMessage: Taxonomy recorded. Classification now has the governed categories to map against.
editorHelper: One row per governed category - definitions matter.

intro.heading: Before you classify: the category tree

sections.title: A taxonomy, not free text
sections.body: What a ticket can be is not open-ended. It maps to a governed set of categories the Support Ops Analyst owns. Free-text labels fracture reporting; a taxonomy keeps every ticket comparable.

sections.title: Definitions do the work
sections.body: The category name is not enough - its definition is what a classifier applies. 'Outage: service down for many users' is a testable rule; 'outage' alone is a guess.

sections.title: Owned and versioned
sections.body: The Support Ops Analyst owns the taxonomy, and changes are governed. When misroutes pile up, the fix is a proposed taxonomy change - not agents inventing their own labels.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A recorded taxonomy classification maps against. Later, the archive loop tunes it from real misroutes.

fieldGuide.meaning: The governed definition a classifier applies.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd keep a short list of categories with clear definitions and map every ticket to one of them, not to ad-hoc labels.

tools.powerAutomate: a reference list of categories and definitions
tools.zapier: a lookup table of the taxonomy
tools.python: a dict of category -> definition loaded at classify time

takeaway.heading: Taxonomy recorded
